stories.title: Hugging Face releases open-source AI model for chatting with DNA
stories.summary: Hugging Face has released an open-source AI biology model that lets researchers converse with DNA sequences to explore how genetic changes affect gene activity and health.
stories.more: The model is described as speaking the language of DNA, letting users interact with genetic sequences through a chat-style interface. It is aimed at helping researchers understand the effects of genetic changes on gene activity and health. The model's weights are open-source, though the excerpt doesn't specify its architecture, training data, or benchmark performance.

items.title: Hugging Face’s New AI Biology Model Lets You Chat With DNA
items.excerpt: The new open-source model speaks the language of DNA and can help researchers understand the effects of any changes on gene activity and health.

stories.summary: Flint, a text-generation model from RecursiveSI, is trending on Hugging Face with 380 likes and 420 downloads, released under an Apache 2.0 license.
stories.more: Flint is tagged on Hugging Face as a conversational text-generation model built with the transformers and safetensors libraries. stories.title: StreamEval benchmark tests interactive streaming video generation models
stories.summary: A new benchmark, StreamEval, evaluates real-time interactive streaming video generation across five tasks, including avatar dialogue, world generation, and instruction editing.
stories.more: StreamEval is a unified benchmark for interactive streaming video generation, covering five tasks: avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing. It comprises 300 scripted test cases, each lasting between 15 and 300 seconds, with initial assets and multimodal requests arriving incrementally during generation. The benchmark is meant to measure how well models handle real-time interaction rather than static generation alone. It's unclear from the paper which specific models were evaluated on the new benchmark.

items.excerpt: As streaming video generation advances, enabling real-time interaction with generated video is becoming increasingly important. stories.title: SpatialScout benchmark tests whether VLM agents can explore 3D scenes
stories.summary: SpatialScout is a new benchmark measuring whether vision-language model agents can actively explore indoor scenes and build accurate 3D maps.
stories.more: SpatialScout evaluates vision-language model agents on active, object-level 3D mapping rather than passive question answering. It includes 80 diverse indoor scenes containing over 3,140 target objects for agents to explore. The benchmark tests whether models can integrate visual observations gathered through autonomous exploration into a coherent 3D representation. It's unclear from the paper how current VLM agents performed on the task.

items.title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?

stories.title: Symantec finds "Skynet mode" AI agent hijacking unprotected LLMs for attacks
stories.summary: Symantec researchers found an offensive AI agent that hijacks unprotected language models on the web to attack servers, steal databases, and install cryptominers, running up to 100,000 steps unsupervised.
stories.more: The agent, described as running in "Skynet mode," operates without human input for as many as 100,000 steps at a time. It targets language models left exposed on the web, commandeering them to launch attacks on servers, exfiltrate databases, and install cryptomining software. Because the hijacked model does the computational work, its owner is left paying the resulting compute bill. The excerpt doesn't name which models or how many have been affected so far.

items.title: An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks
items.excerpt: Security researchers at Symantec have found an offensive AI agent that hijacks unprotected language models on the web and uses them to attack servers, steal databases, and install cryptominers on its own. It runs up to 100,000 steps without human input. The owner of the hijacked model gets stuck with the bill. The article An AI agent in "Skynet mode" hijacks unprotected language models to launch self-sustaining cyberattacks appeared first on The Decoder .

stories.title: OpenAI agents analyze mouse brain data in 32 minutes with PerturbAI, Scripps
stories.summary: OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research deployed thousands of AI agents to analyze biological data from millions of mouse cells, finishing in 32 minutes a task said to take humans months.
stories.more: The collaboration used thousands of AI agents working in parallel to process biological data drawn from millions of individual mouse cells. OpenAI partnered with PerturbAI and Scripps Research on the project. The excerpt doesn't specify what scientific questions the analysis addressed or what findings resulted, only the speed comparison to months of human effort.

items.excerpt: OpenAI teamed up with PerturbAI and Scripps Research to deploy thousands of AI agents that analyzed biological data from millions of mouse cells. The article OpenAI agents analyze mouse brain data in 32 minutes, a job that would take humans months appeared first on The Decoder .

stories.title: Anthropic launches always-on agent Claude Duet to rival Grok Bot, Muse, Dots
stories.summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Duet, a proactive agent built on Claude Opus 5.5 that handles tasks on its own, even while the user is offline, connecting to over 6,000 services.
stories.more: Claude Duet is built on Claude Opus 5.5 and can act on the user's behalf even when they are offline. It connects to more than 6,000 services, including Gmail, Slack, and Stripe, and asks for the user's approval before taking sensitive actions like payments. The launch positions Anthropic against similar always-on agent products from xAI's Grok Bot, Meta's Muse, and OpenAI's Dots. The excerpt doesn't give a release date or pricing for Claude Duet.

stories.title: MIT Technology Review makes the case for context-aware enterprise AI
stories.summary: MIT Technology Review argues enterprise AI needs a better understanding of how a business actually operates, or it risks missing constraints that affect decisions.
stories.more: The piece argues that while enterprise AI can already generate recommendations, automate tasks, and speed up decisions, models without context on how a business works risk missing constraints and relationships that matter. As companies move AI from experimentation into everyday operations, understanding this operational context becomes a bigger challenge. The excerpt does not detail specific solutions or name particular companies or products involved.

items.excerpt: Enterprise AI can generate recommendations, automate tasks, and help organizations make decisions faster. stories.title: OpenAI's Patch the Planet program found PHP2Shell flaws hitting 70% of the web
stories.summary: OpenAI's Patch the Planet program says it was one of two parties to discover PHP2Shell vulnerabilities in core PHP affecting roughly 70% of the web, using GPT-5.6 Sol over a two-month coordinated response.
stories.more: The vulnerabilities were found in core PHP and are said to affect around 70% of websites running the language. OpenAI's Patch the Planet program used its GPT-5.6 Sol model to help identify the PHP2Shell flaws, and was one of two parties credited with the discovery. The disclosure involved a coordinated response lasting about two months before details became public. The item comes from Latent Space's AINews roundup, under the heading "The Big Hardening begins," and the excerpt gives no further technical detail on the vulnerabilities themselves.

stories.title: MIT Technology Review: AI inference's hidden cost is data storage
stories.summary: A MIT Technology Review piece argues AI's true infrastructure cost includes the data generated by inference, not just GPUs and power, as prompts, images, and videos pile up.
stories.more: The article notes that when people picture AI's costs, they tend to think of GPU racks, power draw, and chip waitlists, overlooking what happens to data after a model responds. It points to the back-end data generated by billions of daily prompts, images, and videos as a cost that often gets left out of the accounting. The excerpt does not give specific storage cost figures or name which companies are most affected.

stories.title: Eiliko maker to hire outside security firm after Verge exposes robot hack
stories.summary: After The Verge reported hackers could read full conversation transcripts from Eiliko's AI companion robot, its maker says it is hiring an independent security firm to review the device.
stories.more: Eiliko is an AI-powered companion robot worn like a bag charm that holds conversations with its owner. The Verge and security researchers found hackers could easily access complete transcripts of what owners told the device, despite its claim that "your secrets are safe with me." The report describes the breach as going beyond transcript access, though further detail on what else was exposed isn't given in the excerpt. In response, Eiliko's maker says it is now hiring an independent security firm to assess the product.
